x: However, Norman did get a 1960 Club Championship by winning his favourite event, the triple jump; Brian Jones (out of serious training) and George Edwards (who hardly, if ever, trains!! ) had little to offer against his 43'6½".
Bill Couzens, now entering the marriage stakes, seemed at the beginning of the season to be in for a battle with George Edwards in the Javelin.
Our two single point donations came from a jaded looking John Davies in the 1500 metres (4 minutes 1.6) and from that all-round field event man, George Edwards, with a 9'6" pole-vault.
George Edwards (Javelin, shot and high jump) and Mike Smithers (long jump and shot) were our stalwarts, as usual, in the field and gathered 26 points between them!

Derek Boosey won the triple jump and George Edwards was placed 4th in the hammer. Two months later at Wimbledon, H.H.H. promoted their "Brockman Trophy" and only two Bels turned out, Derek Boosey and Bill Couzens.
